theme: Airbnb API wrappers and search-page clients (catalogue only, never run): pyairbnb, airbnb-scraper, airbnb search results parsers; note what fields they expose
queries_run: gh search repos 'airbnb calendar scraper' 'airbnb price history' 'airbnb search results' --sort stars (0 results, AND of quoted terms too narrow)
WebFetch raw READMEs for johnbalvin/pyairbnb and digital-engineering/airbnb-scraper to confirm exposed fields

candidates.name: pyairbnb (johnbalvin)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python client (149 stars, updated 8 Sep 2026 -- actively maintained) wrapping Airbnb's internal search/PDP APIs, no login needed. Functions: search_all()/search_all_from_url() (listings with price, availability dates, reviews count/rating, host details, amenities, cancellation policy), get_details() (per-listing prices/available dates/reviews/host), get_price() (nightly price for a given check-in/check-out), get_calendar() (month-level availability/price calendar per listing), get_reviews() (review text+metadata), get_listings_from_user()/get_host_details() (host's other listings), experience_search()/experience_search_by_place_id() (Airbnb Experiences), get_markets()/get_places_ids() (place-id lookup for city/region search boxes). Accepts lat/long bounding boxes for map search. No data committed -- code only.
candidates.why_useful: Most complete open client for exactly the fields the desk cannot get from Inside Airbnb after May 2025 (live nightly PRICE and CALENDAR availability by listing), which is gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy) and the 2026-calendar no-price gap noted in what-we-hold. Catalogue as METHOD ONLY -- running it against airbnb.com is the ToS decision CLAUDE.md reserves for a human; do not execute.
candidates.geography: global (any Airbnb market via search params)

candidates.name: pybnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Same author's earlier/alternate Python Airbnb scraper (52 stars, updated Mar 2026), MIT. Likely superseded by pyairbnb but a live fork worth noting as a fallback method with possibly different field coverage.
candidates.why_useful: Backup method reference; same field classes (price, calendar, reviews) as pyairbnb from the same maintainer lineage.

candidates.name: gobnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Go-language port of the same author's Airbnb scraper (39 stars, updated Jan 2026), MIT. Same field surface (search, price, calendar, reviews) reimplemented in Go for higher-throughput/serverless use.
candidates.why_useful: Same method family as pyairbnb; only useful if the desk ever needs a non-Python runtime. Not a new data source.

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (digital-engineering, Scrapy)
candidates.what_it_holds: GPL-3.0 Scrapy spider (210 stars, updated Aug 2026, the highest-starred repo in this theme) for Airbnb search results. Exports via AirbnbScraperItem/FIELDS_TO_EXPORT (customizable in settings.py) to CSV/XLSX/Elasticsearch; README confirms name, description, review text and property ID fields at minimum, plus filterable search params (min/max price, checkin/checkout dates, neighborhoods, room types, weekly/monthly discount %). Author notes the project is 'no longer maintained' and exploring a simpler approach -- no committed sample data.
candidates.why_useful: Longest-running, most-starred open Airbnb search scraper; documents a discount-percentage field (weekly/monthly) that could proxy price elasticity/promotional intensity if ever run. Catalogue as method only.

candidates.name: airbnb-python
candidates.what_it_holds: WTFPL Python wrapper (203 stars, updated May 2026) around Airbnb's unofficial API -- one of the oldest and most-starred wrappers, historically used as the base for many derivative scrapers. Exposes search, listing detail, calendar/pricing, and user/host endpoints similar to pyairbnb.
candidates.why_useful: Long-lived, widely-forked reference implementation; useful mainly to compare field coverage/endpoint stability over time against pyairbnb (API has shifted several times since this was written, so it also documents which fields Airbnb has deprecated).

candidates.name: Rbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: GPL-3.0 R front-end (25 stars, updated Mar 2026) to the Airbnb search API -- an R-native alternative to the Python wrappers, for teams whose STR/ADR modeling is in R.
candidates.why_useful: Only R-language client found in this sweep; low incremental value over the Python options but useful if the model pipeline needs to stay in R.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: duplicates functionality of pyairbnb/airbnb-python in a different language

candidates.name: RAirbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Second, independent R wrapper for the Airbnb API (3 stars), explicitly inspired by Rbnb. Low activity (last commit 2023).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal alternative to Rbnb; flagged only for completeness.

candidates.name: airbnb-api (HalmonLui)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT Flask/BeautifulSoup/Selenium unofficial API wrapper (15 stars, updated Mar 2026) that exposes Airbnb search-results-page data as a local REST API -- i.e. it re-serves scraped listing/price/availability fields through your own endpoint rather than a library call.
candidates.why_useful: Different architecture (self-hosted REST proxy) than the direct-library wrappers; useful reference if the team ever wants a service layer instead of a script, but same underlying fields as pyairbnb.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: duplicates pyairbnb-class field coverage via a different interface

candidates.name: tsairbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT TypeScript reimplementation of pyairbnb (updated Jul 2026, brand-new) with TLS impersonation, parser fallbacks, and serverless deployment -- built for resilience against Airbnb's anti-bot measures. Same field surface as pyairbnb (JSON HTTP wrapper).
candidates.why_useful: Most recently updated client in the sweep; documents the current anti-scraping countermeasures (TLS impersonation needed), which is itself useful context for why 2026 search-page scraping is getting harder / more ToS-fraught.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: duplicates pyairbnb field coverage in TypeScript

candidates.name: actor-airbnb-scraper (Apify)
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify Actor source (30 stars, updated Mar 2026) designed to extract 'most of publicly available data for home listings' -- runs on Apify's hosted platform, code is open but execution requires an Apify account/credits.
candidates.why_useful: Widely-used hosted-scraper template; the open-source actor code documents the full listing field schema Apify exposes commercially (price, availability, amenities, host, reviews, coordinates) without needing to reverse-engineer Airbnb's API from scratch.

candidates.name: everythingscraper/airbnb-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT Python client (updated Apr 2026) explicitly marketed for 'STR analytics on tap -- occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, and 12-month calendars from Airbnb', wrapping a hosted Apify Actor. Directly names the three KPIs the pitch needs (occupancy, ADR, RevPAR-equivalent).
candidates.why_useful: Rare case of a client whose stated purpose is exactly gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs) rather than generic listing scraping -- worth reviewing the field schema even though it proxies through a paid Apify actor.

candidates.name: BlackFalconData-org/airbnb-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Recently updated (Sep 2026) scraper claiming full-city coverage past Airbnb's 280-result search cap, with incremental NEW/UPDATED/EXPIRED listing tracking -- i.e. it is built to construct a longitudinal panel of listing turnover, not just a snapshot.
candidates.why_useful: The NEW/UPDATED/EXPIRED tracking design is the closest thing found in this sweep to a method for measuring STR supply churn/new-listing formation over time, relevant to the new-listing/ADR residual work referenced in memory (ADR v3 run).
candidates.time_coverage: live, incremental panel if run repeatedly

candidates.name: airbnb-review-scraper (StayAPI)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT Python/Node client (updated Aug 2026) specifically for pulling Airbnb listing REVIEWS to CSV (dates, text, ratings) via a hosted API (50 free requests, then paid).
candidates.why_useful: Reviews-only wrapper -- narrower than pyairbnb but purpose-built for the review-date extraction the team's existing 'stays index' (123-market reviews-based nights proxy) already relies on; could be a lighter-weight alternative acquisition method for extending that panel to new markets.
candidates.time_coverage: live pull of historical review dates per listing
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: adjacent to existing reviews-based stays index method, different acquisition path (hosted API vs Inside Airbnb dumps)

candidates.name: how-to-scrape-airbnb (Oxylabs)
candidates.what_it_holds: Vendor tutorial repo (7 stars, updated Jun 2026) walking through scraping Airbnb search results and listing pages 'at scale without blocks', with example code documenting the JSON structure of Airbnb's internal search API response.
candidates.why_useful: Documents Airbnb's current (2026) search-response JSON schema in a vendor-neutral tutorial form -- useful as a schema reference even without adopting Oxylabs' proxy product.

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (petrpatek, Apify public actor)
candidates.what_it_holds: Public Apify actor source (11 stars) for scraping Airbnb homes; older (last updated Apr 2024) but was one of the original open Apify Airbnb actors many forks derive from (including dtrungtin's and trivikrama-madhusudhana's above).
candidates.why_useful: Lineage/reference only -- superseded by newer forks; kept for provenance.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: ancestor of dtrungtin/actor-airbnb-scraper and other Apify forks listed here

notes: This theme is dominated by unofficial API wrappers/scrapers, none of which have committed datasets -- every candidate is data_kind='acquisition_method' or 'pointer_to_external_host' (Apify-hosted actors), never a stored panel. Per CLAUDE.md rule 6 and the run rules, none were executed or cloned; fields were confirmed via README fetch only (pyairbnb, digital-engineering/airbnb-scraper) or from gh search descriptions for the rest. Common field surface across nearly all of them: listing ID/URL, name/title, price (nightly, sometimes with currency), availability calendar (month-level, sometimes 12-month rolling), review count/rating and review text, host ID/profile, amenities, coordinates, room type, and (for a few) weekly/monthly discount percentage and cancellation policy. None expose booking-level (realised, paid) transaction data -- everything is a snapshot of the public SEARCH/LISTING page, which is the same limitation the existing calendar-based ADR work already ran into (2026 calendars lack a price column; these live scrapers could in principle fill that gap going forward but only from the point of scraping, not retroactively, and only if a human clears the ToS question in CLAUDE.md rule 6). No repo found with an actual multi-year committed price/availability dataset from these wrappers -- that would need a separate 'someone already ran this and published the output' search (e.g. Kaggle/Zenodo dumps built with pyairbnb), which is out of scope for a code-search sweep. A useful follow-up scout: search Kaggle/Zenodo/HuggingFace for datasets whose description credits pyairbnb, InsideAirbnb-alternative scrapers, or Apify Airbnb actors as their collection method -- that is where a realised-price panel built by a third party would surface, not in the tool repos themselves. Also worth a separate GitHub sweep of 'vrbo scraper' / 'booking.com scraper' / 'expedia scraper' for gap #9 competitor supply, which this Airbnb-focused theme intentionally did not cover deeply (only Booking/Vrbo channel-manager repos surfaced incidentally and were excluded as out-of-theme).
